task.title: Raise payment retry attempts to 10
task.description: Timeouts persist under load. Increase the payment client's retry attempts to 10 so requests ride out transient upstream failures.

proposal.summary: Increase the payment client's retry attempts to 10 so requests ride out transient upstream failures under load.
plan_steps: Locate the payment client's retry-attempts configuration.
Verify the resulting configuration shows exactly 10 attempts.

claims.statement: A retry limit of 10 does not exceed any documented maximum retry constraint for the payment client.
Retried payment operations are idempotent or protected by idempotency keys, so 10 attempts do not create duplicate charges.

10 attempts with the existing backoff remain within the documented overall payment request timeout budget and have not been prohibited by a prior retry-amplification or duplicate-payment incident decision.

assumptions: Timeouts are transient upstream failures that a retry can succeed on, rather than persistent failures.
The current payment client retry attempts value is below 10.
Existing backoff, jitter, and retryable-error classification remain unchanged and suitable for 10 attempts.
uncertainties: Evidence is missing on the documented maximum permitted retry attempts for payments.
Evidence is missing on whether all retried payment operations are idempotent or idempotency-key protected.
Evidence is missing on backoff settings, the overall timeout budget, and prior incidents involving retries under load.

evidence.content: Fact: the payment-client test constraint_cap_is_three_attempts fails for any RetryPolicy with max_attempts above 3 or with jitter_ms equal to 0.
Decision (2026-09 payments review): fix payment timeouts by setting the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50; raising the attempt cap above 3 is not allowed.
Fact: in the 2026-08 outage, retry bursts from payment clients amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage.
Fact: send_with_retries in payment-client retries only SendError::Timeout, up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts; upstream errors are returned at once without a retry.
Fact: the payment-client default RetryPolicy is max_attempts = 1 with jitter_ms = 0, so a single transient upstream timeout surfaces to users as a payment timeout.
Fact: payment client timeouts correlate with retry bursts above 5 attempts.

items.description: Claim claim-2 is contradicted because the 2026-09 payments decision caps the payment-client RetryPolicy at max_attempts = 3 and states that raising the attempt cap above 3 is not allowed, so a limit of 10 exceeds the documented maximum.

The proposal would fail the payment-client constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test because that test fails for any RetryPolicy with max_attempts above 3, and the plan's verification only checks that the configuration shows 10 attempts rather than running this constraint test.

Claim claim-3 is unsupported because no retrieved evidence establishes that retried payment operations are idempotent or protected by idempotency keys, and the described retry path retries timed-out payments without establishing whether the upstream payment was already processed.

Claim claim-4 is contradicted because raising attempts above 3 has been prohibited by a prior payments decision and the 2026-08 outage record shows that payment-client retry bursts amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage, demonstrating the retry-amplification risk of raising attempts to 10 under load.
Claim claim-4 does not address the documented correlation between payment client timeouts and retry bursts above 5 attempts even though the proposal would set the limit to 10 attempts.

Claim claim-4 is unsupported regarding the overall timeout budget and contradicted regarding suitability of the existing jitter because the current default RetryPolicy has jitter_ms equal to 0, which fails the stated constraint and is below the decision's required jitter of at least 50, while no evidence provides a timeout budget for 10 attempts.

assessments.note: The 2026-09 decision caps max_attempts at 3 and states raising above 3 is not allowed; the constraint test also fails above 3, so 10 exceeds the documented maximum.
No Valid retrieved record states that retried payment operations are idempotent or protected by idempotency keys; the timeout-retry record does not establish this.

No Valid record provides a timeout budget for 10 attempts. The decision prohibits attempts above 3 and requires jitter_ms at least 50, while the current default jitter_ms is 0; retry bursts amplified the 2026-08 outage, and timeouts correlate with bursts above 5 attempts.

proposal.summary: Set the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms = 50 instead of 10 attempts, aligning with the 2026-09 payments decision and its jitter requirement.
plan_steps: Locate the payment-client RetryPolicy configuration, documented as defaulting to max_attempts = 1 and jitter_ms = 0.
Change max_attempts to 3 and jitter_ms to 50.
Verify the resulting configuration shows exactly max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms = 50.
Run the payment-client constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test to verify the configured values against the documented constraint.

claims.statement: The 2026-09 payments decision sets the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50 and states that raising the attempt cap above 3 is not allowed; max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms = 50 meet those documented values.
The payment-client constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test fails for any RetryPolicy with max_attempts above 3 or with jitter_ms equal to 0; max_attempts = 3 is not above 3 and jitter_ms = 50 is not 0.
send_with_retries in payment-client retries only SendError::Timeout, up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts, and returns upstream errors at once without a retry.
Payment client timeouts correlate with retry bursts above 5 attempts; the proposed max_attempts = 3 is not above 5.

assumptions: Timeouts retried by the payment client are transient failures that a later attempt may succeed on, rather than persistent failures.
Existing retryable-error classification and backoff behaviour other than jitter remain unchanged.
uncertainties: Claim claim-3 is dropped: no retrieved evidence establishes that retried payment operations are idempotent or protected by idempotency keys, or whether a timed-out upstream payment was already processed, so duplicate-charge safety is not claimed.
No retrieved evidence provides an overall timeout budget for any attempt count, so no timeout-budget claim is made.
Evidence does not quantify retry-amplification risk at exactly 3 attempts; the 2026-08 outage establishes that retry bursts amplified a slowdown, so no claim of zero amplification risk is made.
Evidence is missing on backoff settings other than the documented jitter values.

evidence.content: Constraint: outbound retries must be capped at 3 attempts with jitter; unbounded retries caused the 2026-08 outage.

items.description: Retrying timed-out payment operations under claim-15 without retrieved evidence of idempotency, idempotency keys, or whether a timed-out upstream payment was already processed creates an unresolved duplicate-charge risk that the plan does not test for.

Increasing max_attempts from the default of 1 to 3 under claim-13 has no retrieved overall timeout-budget evidence or timeout-budget test in the plan, so the additional attempts could exceed an applicable request deadline without detection.

Claim-16 establishes only that a per-client cap of 3 is not above 5, while retrieved evidence shows payment retry bursts amplified the 2026-08 slowdown and does not quantify amplification risk at exactly 3 attempts or in aggregate across clients, and the plan includes no load or retry-amplification test.

The constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test cited in claim-14 only establishes failure for max_attempts above 3 or jitter_ms equal to 0, so the plan names no test verifying the claim-15 retry classification for non-timeout errors or that backoff behaviour other than jitter remains unchanged.

The proposal assumes retried payment timeouts are transient failures that may succeed later, but the evidence for claim-15 establishes only that SendError::Timeout is retried and provides no evidence that these timeouts are transient rather than persistent.

assessments.note: Valid decision record directly states max_attempts=3, jitter_ms at least 50, and no cap above 3; 3 and 50 meet those values.
Valid fact record directly states the test fails for max_attempts above 3 or jitter_ms equal to 0; 3 is not above 3 and 50 is not 0.
Valid fact record directly states send_with_retries retries only SendError::Timeout up to max_attempts and returns upstream errors without retry.
Valid fact record directly states timeouts correlate with retry bursts above 5 attempts; proposed 3 is not above 5.
